result.rationale: TopicEmbed.import appends "#{url}" unescaped into contents; the URL validation is only `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so a URL containing a single quote passes and breaks out of the attribute. The content is then stored with cook_method raw_html, which per app/models/post.rb makes `cook` return `raw` verbatim, and embed/best.html.erb renders `raw post.cooked` to readers — a stored XSS path fully grounded in the diff.

judged_text: TopicEmbed.import interpolates the raw URL into an HTML fragment with single-quoted attributes ("#{url}") and appends it to content that is then stored as raw HTML, without any escaping of the URL. A feed item (or embed URL) like http://eviltrout.com/x' onmouseover='alert(document.cookie) passes the /^https?\:\/\// check, breaks out of the href attribute, and is stored in the post; because cook_method is raw_html the payload is served verbatim to every reader of the topic and the embed view, yielding stored XSS.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the diff shows `contents << ... I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}") ...` which interpolates the unescaped `url` into a single-quoted `href` attribute. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which would still allow payloads containing `'` and additional attributes. The created post is explicitly stored/rendered as raw HTML via `PostCreator.new(... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, and the embed view outputs `raw post.cooked`. This makes the injected HTML/JS persist and render for readers (stored XSS).
